Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.description: Everything you need to know before you apply.
Faq.q1a: Anyone aged 16 or older — developers, designers, product managers, and students. All skill levels are welcome.
Faq.q2q: How much does it cost to participate?
Faq.q2a: Participation costs 2,000 KGS per team. We cover meals, workspace, and swag for all accepted participants.
Faq.q3q: Do I need a team to apply?
Faq.q3a: No. You can apply solo and we will help you form a team at the start of the event, or bring your own team of up to 5 people.
Faq.q4a: Bring your laptop, charger, and any hardware you may need for your project. We provide the rest.
Faq.q5a: Anything you like — an app, a website, a hardware prototype, or an AI model. Projects are judged within the event tracks.
Faq.q6a: Projects are evaluated by our jury based on innovation, technical complexity, impact, and presentation.

Terms.title: Terms of Use
Terms.s1Body: By accessing or using the Hackathon 2026 platform, website, and related services, you agree to be bound by these Terms of Use. If you do not agree with any part of these terms, please do not use the platform.
Terms.s2Body: The hackathon is open to participants aged 16 and older. You agree to provide accurate, current, and complete information during registration and to keep your account information up to date.
Terms.s3Body: You may use the platform only for lawful purposes and in accordance with these terms. You agree not to attempt to disrupt, hack, or interfere with the operation of the platform, its servers, or any third-party services.
Terms.s4Body: You retain all rights to your submissions. By submitting a project, you grant the organizers a non-exclusive license to showcase your work during and after the event for promotional purposes.
Terms.s5Body: The platform is provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis. The organizers make no warranties and are not liable for any direct or indirect damages arising from your use of the platform or participation in the event.
Terms.s6Body: We may update these Terms of Use from time to time. Any changes will be posted on this page with an updated revision date. Your continued use of the platform after changes constitutes acceptance.
Terms.s7Body: If you have any questions about these Terms of Use, please contact us at organizers@hackathon.example.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.s1Body: When you register for the hackathon, we collect your name, email address, and primary role. We may also collect technical information such as your IP address and browser type to ensure the platform works correctly.
Privacy.s2Body: We use your information to process registrations, communicate important updates about the event, match you with mentors, and improve the overall experience.
Privacy.s3Body: We do not sell your personal data. We may share it with trusted service providers who help us operate the platform, always under strict confidentiality obligations and only for the purposes described in this policy.
Privacy.s4Body: We retain your personal data for as long as necessary to operate the event and meet legal obligations. When it is no longer needed, your data is securely deleted or anonymized.
Privacy.s5Body: You have the right to access, correct, or delete your personal data at any time. To exercise these rights, contact us using the details below.
Privacy.s6Body: We apply reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect your personal data from unauthorized access, alteration, or loss.
Privacy.s7Body: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or your data, please contact us at privacy@hackathon.example.

Conduct.title: Code of Conduct
Conduct.s1Body: Hackathon 2026 is dedicated to providing a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, religion, sexual orientation, or technical background.
Conduct.s2Body: Be respectful, supportive, and collaborative. Help fellow participants, share knowledge openly, and give credit where it is due.
Conduct.s3Body: Harassment, intimidation, discrimination, and offensive language or imagery are not tolerated. This includes unwelcome sexual attention, trolling, and deliberate disruption of talks or workshops.
Conduct.s4Body: If you are subject to unacceptable behavior or witness any such behavior, please report it to the organizers in person, via email, or through the official event channels.
Conduct.s5Body: Organizers may take any action they deem appropriate, including warning the offender, excluding them from the event, or reporting the incident to the authorities.
Conduct.s6Body: This Code of Conduct applies to all event spaces, including online channels, workshops, and social events, both during and after the hackathon.
